FOREWORD. Message from the Director
I am proud to introduce REA’s 2026 Annual Work Programme, and to outline the priorities and
the challenges we anticipate in the coming year. Once again, we aim to propel the European
Union's research and innovation agenda forward with resilience and ingenuity, building on our
past successes and addressing the evolving needs of the European research and innovation
landscape.
In 2026, REA will continue to implement major parts of the Horizon Europe Research and
Innovation Programme, with a focus on increasing the Union’s productivity and competitiveness
in a circular and environmentally friendly manner, sustaining our socio-economic models and
values, protecting our nature, water, soils and ecosystems and delivering innovative solutions to
address societal challenges. Our work will also extend to the promotion of agricultural products
through the AGRIP programme, and the Research Programme of the Research Fund for Coal
and Steel, both of which contribute to the competitiveness and sustainability of specific
European industries and economic sectors.
The broader context for 2026 presents a dynamic environment, characterised by rapid
technological advancements, such as the wide-scale use of artificial intelligence, an evolving
geopolitical context, and an increased focus on sustainable competitiveness. The current
geopolitical tensions and increasing use of restrictive measures will impact our work, requiring
us to adapt to new requirements and operational constraints. The recast of the Financial
Regulation and the European Economic Security Strategy have reinforced the European Union’s
capacity to implement restrictive measures in EU award procedures concerning security and
public order. As a result, we will see a substantial increase in dual-use topics across funding
programmes, including RFCS, which will require that we adapt our procedures and equip
ourselves to handle the associated complexities.
Simplification remains a top priority for REA, as we strive to reduce administrative burdens and
make it easier for participants to engage with our programmes. However, the increasing volume
of proposals in response to calls presents both a challenge and an opportunity. While this
growth underscores the vibrancy and competitiveness of Europe's research landscape, it
requires streamlined evaluation processes to maintain the satisfaction of applicants. We will
continue to simplify our evaluation procedures, as well as our grant management processes, to
provide the best possible service to our applicants and beneficiaries while preserving our high-
quality standards.
As we look to the future, REA will maintain a close collaboration with the Commission to
prepare for the next generation of funding programmes under the Multiannual Financial
Framework (MFF) 2028-2034. By sharing our expertise and experience, we will contribute to the
development of effective programme implementation modalities and inform the Commission's
cost-benefit analysis, ultimately supporting the successful launch of REA's 4th mandate in
2028.
REA remains committed to delivering results and maximising the impact of the programmes
that we manage. REA's Annual Work Programme 2026 sets out a clear roadmap for achieving
this, and for continuing to foster transformative science benefiting future generations, ensuring
that Europe remains at the forefront of research and innovation excellence.

PART 1. Mission statement
Mandated by the European Commission to support the EU’s research and innovation policy, REA
funds and assists high-quality research and innovation projects that generate knowledge
leading to a greener world, in which Europe has prosperous, inclusive economies and societies
that take full advantage of the digital age.
REA is promoting its mission through the slogan “Fostering excellent science for future
generations”. To pursue this mission, REA undertakes the following activities:
Manage the selection of the proposals to fund, conclude and implement grant
agreements, and enable the take-up of project results – including for effective
policymaking – for:
a. major parts of the Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Programme (2021-2027)
aiming at boosting the Union’s productivity and competitiveness, sustaining our socio-
economic model and values, and enabling innovative and systemic solutions to the
challenges faced by our societies;
b. information provision and promotion measures concerning agricultural products (2021-
2027) (AGRIP) to enhance the competitiveness of the Union’s agricultural sector;
c. the Research Programme of the Research Fund for Coal and Steel (RFCS).
Implement the remaining stages of the grant agreements concluded under
predecessor programmes, and enable the take-up of project results – including for
effective policymaking – for:
a. the Horizon 2020 Research Framework Programme;
b. information provision and promotion measures concerning agricultural products pre-
2021;
c. the Research Programme of the Research Fund for Coal and Steel pre-2021.
Provide administrative and logistical support services:
a. to EU bodies implementing Horizon Europe and other programmes. These services
include planning and support for publication of calls for proposals and contests for
prizes; logistical support for the evaluations, including the management of the
evaluation facility; contracting and payment of independent experts who evaluate
proposals;
b. by operating the single-entry point for participants in grants, prizes and
procurement activities for all EU direct management programmes implemented through
the Single Electronic Data Interchange Area (SEDIA). REA services for SEDIA include:
validation of legal entities, including an assessment of third-country control
over participants for specific programmes (Horizon Europe, Digital Europe, European
Defence Industrial Development Programme and EU Defence Fund); financial capacity
assessment of applicants; and the Research Enquiry Service, which answers
questions on the validation process from participants for all programmes and general
enquiries from citizens on EU research and innovation funding.

REA’s mandate
REA’s responsibilities are outlined in the Commission Decision delegating powers to REA.
Annexes I-VII of the Decision set out in detail the tasks delegated to the Agency by the
European Commission for managing the funding programmes and programme parts it
implements. The Decision entrusts REA with managing the full project lifecycle, based on the
policy priorities and framing conditions stipulated in the Work Programmes or other legal bases
adopted by the Commission for each programme:
• Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 8493 on the Horizon Europe Work
Programme for 2026-2027;
• Commission Implementing Decision C(2025) 8551 on the financing of information
provision and promotion measures concerning agricultural products implemented in the
internal market and in third countries and the adoption of the work programme for
2026;
• Commission Implementing Decision C(2026)757 on the financing of the Research
Programme of the Research Fund for Coal and Steel (RFCS) and the adoption of the
work programme for 2026.
The Agency’s mandate also covers managing the portfolio of running projects financed by the
predecessor programmes of those listed above.
In 2026, REA’s activities will contribute to the achievement of the Commission’s political
priorities for 2025-2029. The connections between the programmes implemented by the
Agency, the objectives of its parent DGs, and the Commission priorities, are shown in Figure 2
below.

A. Horizon Europe and legacy of Horizon 2020
This section highlights aspects that will require particular attention when implementing the
Horizon Europe and Horizon 2020 programmes. Details on expected outputs per programme
part in 2026 can be found in the performance tables in Annex 1.
Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA)
MSCA aims to enhance the skills and employability of researchers at all career stages through
international and intersectoral mobility, promoting innovative training and attractive career
opportunities across Europe.
In 2026, REA will launch and implement five MSCA calls for proposals with a total budget of
approximately EUR 1 217 million. It is expected that approximately 8 000 researchers will
benefit from the 2026 calls funded through this competitive and prestigious programme.
Achieving key performance targets in 2026 will require significant resources due to the
increased number of proposals and grant agreements. To address this challenge, REA will
work with the Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture (DG EAC) and the
Common Implementation Centre (CIC) of DG RTD to further streamline its processes, in
particular the MSCA evaluation system.
The MSCA Choose Europe for Science pilot will take up the challenge to make research
careers in Europe more attractive by offering excellent working conditions and long-term
prospects. It will allow successful host organisations to employ postdoctoral researchers for up
to five years, ensuring more stable career pathways. The call budget for the pilot is EUR 22.5
million.
Another pilot, RAISE Doctoral Networks, will be introduced alongside MSCA Doctoral Networks,
offering better chances of funding for consortia applying with a research project related to AI in
science (3). This initiative supports the European AI in Science Strategy, which will make the EU
a world-class hub for AI and ensure that AI is human-centric and trustworthy.
The results of a new study on the added value of MSCA Doctorates, part of the MSCA feedback
to policy plan, will be presented and discussed at a networking event, scheduled for 16 and 17
June 2026.
REA will continue to organise training sessions dedicated to MSCA National Contact Points
(NCPs) and will continue its successful industry outreach efforts to encourage increased non-
academic participation in MSCA.
In 2026, MSCA will celebrate its 30th anniversary with a year-long campaign featuring EU-
wide and local events, and digital outreach. The celebration will raise awareness among
policymakers by showcasing the excellence of MSCA-supported projects and their contributions
to research, innovation, society, and European competitiveness. Coordinated by DG EAC in close

Research infrastructures
This programme part supports the development and integration of world-class research
infrastructures across Europe, facilitating access for researchers and fostering collaboration
across disciplines and sectors.
In 2026, REA will initiate the implementation of the 2026 call while completing the
evaluation of the 2025 call. The 2025 call was the largest to date, with a budget of EUR 400.5
million covering 18 topics. It is expected to result in 75 projects to be signed by May.
The 2026 call is set to open in March, with a submission deadline in June. The Info Day will
take place in March 2026. The call has a projected budget of EUR 294.5 million and aims to
fund 40 projects across 12 topics. It features a significant EUR 32 million grant supporting the
eBRAINS infrastructure to provide transnational access. Additionally, it includes a EUR 40 million
grant offering financial support to third parties, which will focus on promoting open science and
effective research data management practices, while advancing a user-focused, science-driven
European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) Federation. In 2026 the EOSC Federation build-up will
continue to integrate the national and thematic EOSC Nodes established through the projects
selected in the 2025 call. Furthermore, the call includes pilots for large thematic clusters of
research infrastructures (EUR 40 million) aiming to develop a single portfolio of complementary
services, in line with the European Strategy on Research and Technology Infrastructures.
Cluster 2: culture, creativity and inclusive society.
This cluster focuses on fostering social resilience and inclusivity through research in cultural
heritage, arts, and social sciences, aiming to strengthen democratic governance, societal
participation, and cultural diversity.
2026 marks a critical phase in implementing the European Partnership for Resilient
Cultural Heritage with the partnership initiation scheduled for the second half of the year. In
addition, preparations will commence for the European Partnership on Social
Transformations and Resilience, which is set to launch in the second half of 2027 with
projected funding of up to EUR 200 million. This funding involves contributions from Member
States, Associated Countries, and the European Commission (30%).
In March, REA will host the Coordinators’ Day for the 10 tools funded from the European
Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage (ECCCH) 2024 call, including the established
ECHOES platform and projects from past calls. The ECCCH initiative will align and integrate
these projects while preparing to support future use cases funded by the 2025 call.
In 2026, REA will be involved in major policy areas identified by DGs RTD, EMPL, and EAC,
including the Democracy Shield, Education and skills, Intergenerational fairness strategy, silver
economy initiatives, the Social Economy Action Plan, EU Migration R&I, and SSH integration, as

well as initiatives related to the Quality Jobs Act, the European Anti-Poverty Strategy, the just
transition, and the Action Plan on the Implementation of the European Pillar of Social Rights. A
Feedback-to-Policy plan is under preparation, ensuring that REA provides insights from its
portfolio of funded projects in direct support of these policy initiatives.
Cluster 3: civil security for society
Dedicated to enhancing resilience and security, this cluster addresses challenges such as
disaster risk reduction, protection of critical infrastructure, effective management of EU external
borders , and fighting crime and terrorism through innovative solutions and collaborative
research.
REA will continue to utilise its expertise in (civil) security research to ensure effective
evaluation and monitoring of projects funded under Cluster 3. Particular attention will be given
to the implementation of the rules for handling EU Classified Information (EUCI) within any
EU programme or activity and to the efficient handling of a rising number of Access to
Documents requests.
In 2026, REA will evaluate 19 topics under a single call launched in 2025. This evaluation is
expected to result in an estimated 45 projects selected for funding, a higher number than in
previous years. A streamlined evaluation methodology is envisaged to manage a higher volume
of proposals.
REA will continue to strengthen cooperation between the Directorate-General for Migration and
Home Affairs (DG HOME) and project beneficiaries through the organisation of dedicated events
and the provision of structured policy feedback.
A key ongoing challenge in Cluster 3 is transferring research results into tangible
products and solutions. To address this, REA along with DG HOME seeks the active
involvement of end-users, including law enforcement agencies, customs authorities, and first
responders. Through collaboration and feedback loops, these stakeholders will continue to
contribute with valuable insights, ensuring that the research is aligned with real-world needs.
This is expected to boost the impact and uptake of results, ultimately driving their deployment.
Cluster 6: food, bioeconomy, natural resources, agriculture
and environment
This cluster aims to ensure resilient and sustainable management of natural resources and
ecosystems, addressing food security, climate change, and biodiversity through integrated
approaches.
REA will conduct evaluations in seven calls (three of which are two-stage) covering the
seven Cluster 6 Destinations, with deadlines scheduled for spring and autumn 2026. These
evaluation sessions will include a significant number of lump sum topics and blind evaluations
for most first stage topics.
The Agency expects an increased emphasis on biodiversity topics in the last years of Horizon
Europe, with additional budget allocation and topics in Cluster 6 in 2026 and in 2027.

The implementation of co-funded European Partnerships will continue in 2026, building on
the success of the previous eight partnerships funded under Cluster 6. The associated grants
will focus on Biodiversity, Blue Economy, Water4All, Agroecology, Animal Health and Welfare,
Sustainable Food Systems, and Agriculture of Data. A new European Partnership on Forests
and Forestry for a Sustainable Future will be launched, complementing the existing
partnerships with Member States and Associated Countries. These partnerships are driving
policy development and ensuring a consistent research and innovation agenda for European
and national funding.
REA will implement the Cluster 6 Feedback to Policy plan together with the Commission. This
plan ensures that research results are used to support different DGs in EU priority policy areas.
Overall, REA expects to participate in around 100 different communication and/or Feedback
to Policy events in 2026 in support of Cluster 6, ranging from cluster meetings to policy
workshops and conferences.
Widening participation and spreading excellence
This programme part seeks to reduce disparities in R&I across Europe by promoting
participation from widening countries (i.e. EU Member States and Associated Countries that
have lower R&I performance), thereby fostering a more inclusive European Research Area.
In 2026, REA will build on its previous work under Horizon 2020 by continuing to manage
initiatives such as ERA Chairs, Twinning, and Teaming. Additionally, REA will oversee the
implementation of new actions introduced under Horizon Europe, including Excellence Hubs,
the European Excellence Initiative (EEI), ERA Talents, and Pathway to Synergies.
REA will monitor the new Dissemination & Exploitation Action and to manage the European
Co-Operation in Science and Technology (COST) programme.
Furthermore, the Agency will work on seven separate evaluations and two new actions: the
Research Management Facility and TEAMING Synergies. In addition, record submissions are
expected for TWINNING, for which REA will pilot a more streamlined evaluation process.
Reforming and enhancing the European R&I system
This programme part focuses on strengthening the European Research Area by promoting
research policy reforms, improving R&I governance, and supporting transformative changes in
research practices across the EU.
REA will launch the 2026 ERA call, supporting the second ERA Policy Agenda 2025-2027. In
2026, approximately 50 new grant agreements will be signed (20 from the 2025 call, 25 from
the 2026 call closing in March, and five new Identified Beneficiary Actions).
Communication and outreach will remain an important focus. REA will emphasise how projects
advance the priorities of the ERA Policy Agenda 2025–2027, using the ERA Policy Platform and
a variety of complementary communication tools. The Agency will also be involved in convening
cluster events.

The Agency will support the fifth edition of the EU Award for Gender Equality Champions,
organised by DG RTD. The Award is starting to build a critical mass of excellent Gender Equality
Plans across the EU R&I ecosystem.
REA will play a role in enhancing coherence and mutual reinforcement among initiatives linked
to higher education, artificial intelligence, and research careers. Particular attention will be
given to promoting the ethical deployment of AI, research ethics and innovation ecosystems,
advancing researchers’ skills and career development, open science and research assessment
reform, and encouraging cross-disciplinary collaboration and knowledge circulation within
Europe’s research and innovation system.
REA will continue to manage several actions initiated in 2025 that directly
support policy activities in the European Research Area and Research
Infrastructures. These include grants for the OAPEN initiative, supporting the
European Union's Open Access policy; the EU Open Research Repository; the
activities of the European Group on Ethics; and the development and uptake of
Ethics and Integrity Promotion Plans and Standard Operating Procedures.
Additionally, the flagship Open Research Europe, a non-profit open access
scientific publishing service, has received a €10 million grant to support its long-
term continuation and operations.

Contribution to EU Missions
EU Missions are large-scale initiatives under Horizon Europe setting clear, time-bound goals
that drive focused efforts towards some of our greatest challenges. They aim to deliver
concrete results by 2030. Research and innovation play a pivotal role in achieving these goals
through Horizon Europe.
REA contributes to multiple EU Missions across calls and topics and is a member of the
Mission Owners Groups where key activities and Work Programme priorities are discussed.
The Agency will continue to provide feedback on policy aspects related to the EU Missions.
A Soil Deal for Europe
REA plays a crucial role in the development and implementation of the "A Soil Deal for Europe"
Mission. As part of its responsibilities, REA evaluates and implements the Mission's research
and innovation component. Currently, there are 62 ongoing projects, including nine specific
projects that have established 45 Living Labs, with a target of 100 Living Labs by 2030. The
first Living Labs projects will undergo their first review in 2026. 17 more projects are expected
to be funded from the 2025 calls (second stage is scheduled in early 2026), and another topic
targeting Living Labs will be conducted in 2026.

To support the successful implementation of the Mission, REA is preparing the continuation of
the Mission Soil Platform (4) and will continue to manage the contract of the Platform in 2026.
The Agency will also continue to focus on clustering activities of the Mission Soil projects,
ensuring effective collaboration and knowledge sharing among stakeholders.
Throughout 2026, REA will participate in various events to share results, facilitate cooperation
between projects, and provide feedback. The European Mission Soil Week, the Mission's main
annual event, will be a key focus of efforts in 2026.
Furthermore, REA will support the implementation of joint calls, including the projects funded

2026. The Agency will also explore strategic collaborations to leverage capabilities and

Cross-cutting actions of EU Missions in the area of social
innovation and for capacity building in the research and
innovation ecosystem
REA contributes to cross-cutting actions of the EU Missions around social innovation. As
a follow-up to the ‘A European Social Innovation Advisory Network in support of EU Mission
Objectives’ call launched in 2024, REA will implement the first project.
Seven projects are devoted to collectively strengthen social innovation, capacity building,
and collaborative governance within Europe’s research and innovation ecosystems,
translating Mission goals into locally driven action. Collectively, these initiatives will advance the
EU’s Mission-oriented innovation agenda in 2026 by embedding citizen participation and
social innovation in R&I activities, building institutional and territorial capacities for Mission
delivery, enhancing cross-sector collaboration and knowledge transfer, and promoting inclusive,
equitable, and sustainable transformations across Europe.
REA will continue to support other Missions, especially the Mission Restore our Oceans
and Waters and the Mission Adaptation to Climate Change, by providing feedback from
relevant research projects in its portfolio, including MSCA projects.

C. Promotion of Agricultural Products
The overarching goal of the EU's Information provision and promotion measures concerning
agricultural products (AGRIP) programme is to bolster the competitiveness of the EU agricultural
sector. This programme focuses on expanding and consolidating market presence as well as
enhancing consumer awareness about the EU's quality standards and schemes, both, within the
EU and globally in third country markets. Additionally, the programme supports sustainable EU
food systems in line with the objectives of the European Green Deal.
AGRIP has been allocated a total budget of EUR 205 million for 2026, with EUR 105 million
managed by REA. In January, two calls for proposals for co-financed programmes—SIMPLE and
MULTI—will be announced, closing in April. Additional calls could be issued in response to
significant market disturbances or declining consumer confidence.

REA will implement the entire lifecycle of MULTI programmes involving consortia with
beneficiaries from multiple Member States, and it will handle the calls, submissions, and
evaluations for SIMPLE programmes, which involve beneficiaries from a single Member
State (5).
In collaboration with the Commission, REA aims to enhance programme participation to
maximise the use of the allocated budget. Given the specific structure of the AGRIP programme,
which relies on subcontracting to execute for-profit promotional campaigns and based on the
results of controls carried out in previous years, REA has refined its control strategies,
incorporating additional ex-ante checks during grant preparations and close monitoring of
the tender procedures. This reinforced control strategy will continue in 2026.
REA is responsible for executing public procurement contracts for promotional activities outside
Europe, which include various engagements such as high-level missions, business delegation
visits, and participation in trade fairs to support exports of EU agricultural products. As
announced by President von der Leyen in her State of the Union address, in 2026 REA will
launch a campaign within the EU, for EU agricultural and certain food products. This campaign
has a budget of EUR 35 million.
Supporting the Commission’s policymaking
Scientific evidence is one of the cornerstones of the European Commission’s Better Regulation
process. Successive EU R&I framework programmes, along with other EU-funded research and
innovation activities, offer valuable opportunities for knowledge valorisation and evidence-
based policymaking. REA actively participates in Feedback to Policy (F2P) activities to help
the Commission take advantage of these opportunities.
In 2026, REA will continue to support a broad spectrum of F2P activities based on Commission
needs which are converted into programme-specific F2P plans. These activities range from
providing portfolio lists and policy briefs to policy roundtables and feedback to contributors
drafting Horizon Europe Work Programmes. Beyond the programme-specific F2P activities, REA
intends to invest in:
• assessing and building further F2P capacity within and beyond the Agency by
developing F2P product templates and providing training and supporting peer learning;
• exploring the use of AI to improve policy feedback products and processes;
• connecting REA’s F2P activities to efforts within the Commission and other executive
agencies for evidence-informed policymaking;
• facilitating cross-programme synergy projects linked to Commission priorities.
In the specific area of dissemination and exploitation of project results, REA will engage
with the Commission to develop and promote tools that help EU projects enhance their societal
impact. Furthermore, by providing guidance to beneficiaries on communication and policy
impact, REA will encourage projects to act as multipliers and improve their outreach to EU
citizens, increasing awareness and visibility of EU-funded research and its contribution to
addressing Europe’s societal challenges.

D. Support tasks delegated to the Agency
REA provides support services according to Annex VIII of its Delegation Act (6). REA’s precise
responsibilities are described in a series of Memoranda of Understanding with its clients.
Participant management and management of the Research
Enquiry Service
Through the Central Validation Service (CVS), REA contributes to the implementation of the
Single Electronic Data Interchange Area (SEDIA) by performing the following operations for
participants in EU award procedures:
• Validating legal entities (including the appointment of Legal Entity Appointed
Representatives);
• Creating/modifying their bank account data in the EU accounting tools;
• Preparing the assessment of their financial capacity; and
• Assessing their ownership and control if they participate in EU restricted calls where EU
strategic interests are involved and safeguards against foreign threats are required.
The current Commission has identified the reduction of administrative burden for
businesses and citizens as a key policy priority. In line with this objective, the CVS will pursue
initiatives aimed at simplifying validation processes for external and internal stakeholders. At

Digital transformation
REA is committed to driving digital transformation through a combination of strategic
initiatives. REA’s Digital Transformation Roadmap derives directly from that of the Commission
and addresses four strategic objectives (8).
To enhance its digital culture, REA will promote more awareness among staff of and training
on applications designed to facilitate mobile-ready collaboration, ensuring they are seamlessly
integrated into everyday operations. REA will continue to work on the digital upskilling of its
staff and organise digital trainings and it will maintain high levels of cybersecurity awareness
by encouraging staff to follow corporate training and promoting CyberAware campaigns.
Under business-driven digital transformation, REA - in line with the principles of data
openness and interoperability - will improve business process modelling and automation by
documenting processes and using a business automation platform. REA will promote AI training
and encourage the use of Commission-wide AI solutions, such as GPT@EC, and integrate
existing corporate AI services in its IT systems.
REA is committed to creating a seamless digital environment and a green, secure, and
resilient infrastructure. To achieve this, REA will transform its IT systems by improving their
capabilities and incorporating reusable solutions. REA will also keep upgrading its IT systems to
modern technologies, retain and monitor existing systems, and ensure that they are properly
mapped to business and technical capability models. To promote IT greening, REA will locally
promote information sessions, encourage paperless and energy-saving practices.

data ownership and governance being rolled out by the Commission. Through the participation
in the Results and Data Steering Committee and in the key user groups for the various business
processes, REA will contribute to develop the data management maturity level of all entities
implementing R&I programmes. Priority will be to appoint domain data owners and data
stewards for relevant areas and promote the guidelines developed by the Commission.

processes and IT systems, ensuring consistent and secure handling of data. REA will continue to

C. Sound financial management
REA will continue to implement Horizon Europe grants in line with the ‘Control Strategy for
Horizon Europe’ and the ‘Guidance on Horizon Europe ex-ante controls’. REA remains firmly
committed to its objective of reducing the cumulative representative error rates and
residual error rates (i.e. the amount at risk at closure) of all the programmes it manages
below 2%.
The implementation of lump sum projects will continue to be closely monitored to ensure
that controls are streamlined, and to identify areas for further improvements, efficiency gains
and simplification. This will enable the Agency to evaluate the advantages of this funding
model compared to a process in which actual costs are charged.
As previously mentioned, REA has adapted its AGRIP control strategy to address the risk of
conflict of interest and underperformance in the multi-beneficiary grants part of the AGRIP
programme. This includes reinforced ex-ante checks, a revised risk analysis approach, demands
for bank guarantees, and increased review and control missions. REA will continue to strengthen
requirements and guidance for transparent private tendering in future procedures (e.g.
publication on websites frequented by potential bidders; clearer rules and acceptable practices
presented as widely as possible, including during programme Info Days). These measures will
ensure the effective management of grants and minimise potential risks.

D. Fraud risk management
REA will further implement its Anti-fraud Strategy, updated in 2023, along with its action
plan. Both are in line with the Common Anti-fraud Strategy for Research and Innovation, also
updated in 2023, and the revised Commission Anti-fraud Strategy Action Plan(9).
The actions planned for 2026 will focus on strengthening fraud prevention and detection,
making more effective use of the Early Detection and Exclusion System (EDES) for prevention
and ex-post detection, and coordinating and cooperating across the Agency and with other
services on anti-fraud matters. This will include working closely with the European Anti-Fraud
Office (OLAF) and European Public Prosecutor Office (EPPO) and implementing OLAF
recommendations in a timely manner.
The European Court of Auditors (ECA) audit report on the Commission’s Anti-fraud Strategy is
expected to be released in Q2 2026. The audit may lead to adjustments in REA’s Anti-fraud
Strategy and Action Plan. The preparation of the subsequent Anti-fraud Strategy is also
planned to take place in 2026.
E. Sound environmental management
REA is committed to a sustainable work environment, in line with the Communication
‘Greening the Commission’, and the corresponding Action Plan. Together with the Commission
and other executive agencies, REA takes account of its environmental footprint and actively
promotes measures to reduce the day-to-day environmental impact of its operations. Awaiting
the results of the progress review of the EC’s Greening policy, REA will continue to adhere to the
corporate orientations.
REA will continue to reduce staff/expert travel and to promote alternatives while maintaining
REA’s proximity to programme participants, as well as to set up an efficient tool for monitoring
the carbon footprint of professional travel. REA will maintain the current reduction targets in
2026 for staff/expert emissions (i.e. 50% of emissions generated by staff member in 2019).
The Agency has been a committed partner for the Commission in fostering synergies and
maximising the effectiveness of planned environmental protection activities. Via its EMAS
team, REA will continue its close collaboration with the other executive agencies and the central
EMAS team in the Commission in cross-service actions in 2026 and explore further local actions
in its premises. The ‘Executive Agency (EA) Green Week’ – organised for the third time in 2025 –
has become a showcase of EAs’ close collaboration on ‘greening’ and is expected to continue
for years to come.

C. Delegated operational appropriations
Following the Annex 1 of the Internal Rules for the implementation of the EU General Budget of 2026, REA manages operational appropriations on the
following budget lines. These co-delegated budget lines to REA are mainly used for grant management but can also contain procurement and other
activities. They also include appropriations for experts.
Since 2016, REA uses a single budget line for the management of expert evaluators of the “Horizon” research framework-programmes (i.e., for “Horizon
2020” for the period 2014-2020 and for “Horizon Europe” for the period 2021-2027). This single budget line simplifies the management of REA’s
activities for contracting and paying expert evaluators of Horizon Europe, including for calls not delegated to the Agency (except EURATOM, Direct Actions
and the ERC programmes for which the expert evaluators are not managed by REA). However, the expert reviewers/monitors remain, as previously,
charged to the various budget lines of the delegated programmes.
The expert evaluators for the Joint Undertakings (JUs), the Research Programme of the Research Fund for Coal and Steel (RFCS) and the Promotion of
Agricultural Products (AGRIP) programme, are managed by REA using the appropriate budget lines.
